chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the gallbladder that comes out of a dead kid goat, he said, 'There is no harm with it.' I said, 'The milk that remains in the udder of a sheep after it has died,' he said, 'There is no harm with it.' I said, 'And the wool, the hair, the bones of the elephant, the skin, and the eggs that come out of the hen (after its death),' he said, 'All of this there is no harm with it.'
ai.seo_question: Are the skin, bones, and milk of an animal considered pure if the animal dies without being slaughtered ritually?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of *istihlak* (substantial transformation) and the purity of animal byproducts, ruling that milk, wool, hair, bones, skin, and eggs remain pure even if the source animal dies, provided they are not contaminated by najasah. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the carcass itself (*maytah*) and its constituent parts, which are often considered *tahir* unless explicitly rendered impure by blood or other factors. The narration underscores the practical ease in Islamic law regarding the use of natural animal products, reflecting a nuanced approach to ritual purity (*taharah*) in daily life.
